Part B:
We need the smallest positive integer $x$ such that:
$x \equiv 5 \pmod 9$
$x \equiv 3 \pmod{19}$
$x \equiv 4 \pmod{16}$

From $x \equiv 4 \pmod{16}$:
$x = 16k + 4$.
$16k + 4 \equiv 5 \pmod 9 \implies -2k + 4 \equiv 5 \implies -2k \equiv 1 \implies 7k \equiv 1 \implies k \equiv 4 \pmod 9$.
So $k = 9m + 4$, which gives:
$x = 16(9m + 4) + 4 = 144m + 68$.

Now, modulo 19:
$144m + 68 \equiv 3 \pmod{19}$
$144 = 7 \times 19 + 11 \equiv 11 \pmod{19}$
$68 = 3 \times 19 + 11 \equiv 11 \pmod{19}$
$11m + 11 \equiv 3 \pmod{19}$
$11m \equiv -8 \equiv 11 \pmod{19}$
Dividing by 11 (since $\gcd(11, 19) = 1$):
$m \equiv 1 \pmod{19}$.

The smallest non-negative integer $m$ is 1:
$x = 144(1) + 68 = 212$.
Checking:
$212 = 23 \times 9 + 5$ (remainder 5)
$212 = 11 \times 19 + 3$ (remainder 3)
$212 = 13 \times 16 + 4$ (remainder 4)
